headline: When everything feels like too much—grounding techniques to find calm
universal_truth: Overwhelm is a signal, not a sentence; it passes, and you can help it pass faster
fun_facts: Deep breathing activates the parasympathetic nervous system within 90 seconds
Naming what you feel reduces the intensity of the emotion
Grounding techniques have been used for thousands of years across cultures
discussion_questions: What has helped you calm down in the past?
Who can you reach out to when things feel like too much?

hook.script: You came here because you're overwhelmed. That's okay. This is exactly the right place to be. Let's take a breath together and find some ground beneath your feet.

cliff.script: Overwhelm feels permanent when you're in it. But there are immediate actions that help. What's the first thing to do?

options.text: Breathe and ground—your nervous system needs a reset; slow breathing tells your body you're safe; grounding brings you back to the present moment
options.response: Yes. Right now, take a slow breath. In for 4 counts. Hold for 4. Out for 6. Your body will start to calm. You're safe in this moment.
Analysis comes later. Right now, your nervous system is activated. First, calm the system. Then think...

fact1.title: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding
fact1.script: Try this: Name 5 things you can see. 4 things you can touch. 3 things you can hear. 2 things you can smell. 1 thing you can taste. This pulls you into the present moment.

fact2.title: It Will Pass
fact2.script: Emotions are like weather—they move through. This overwhelming feeling is temporary. You've survived every difficult moment so far. You'll survive this one too.

fact3.title: Reach Out
fact3.script: You don't have to handle everything alone. Reach out to someone you trust. If you're in crisis, contact a helpline. Connection helps more than isolation.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Overwhelm is a signal that you need support—from yourself, from others, from rest. Listen to the signal. Respond with care.

outro.script: How are you feeling now? Even a little better counts. Return to this lesson whenever you need grounding. You're doing better than you think.

growTrack.title: Grounding Practice - Build Your Toolkit
growTrack.activity: Try the 5-4-3-2-1 technique right now. Then, write down 3 things that help you calm down. Keep this list somewhere accessible for future moments of overwhelm.
